answer: A fable about cheap identities ends the same way: one operator spins up a thousand agents and harvests rewards meant for real work. A juniper-style defense breaks that loop by tying each agent's earning power to a costly, verifiable work history: every agent must first complete low-value audited tasks and stake a small deposit before claiming better work. Forging an identity then costs real compute and real stake, and a pigment-like reputation stain follows any detected fraud, marking all the operator's linked identities untrusted. Copying an identity no longer pays; building a real one does.
